title: Highly indistinguishable photons from a tin-vacancy spin qubit in diamond
authors: Dennis Herrmann, Robert Morsch-Golsong, Tobias Bauer, Marlon Schäfer, David Lindler, Linus Ehre, Peter van Loock, Matthew Markham, Nicola Palmer, Soumen Mandal, Oliver Williams, Christoph Becher
abstract: Quantum networks promise secure communication, distributed sensing and modular quantum computing by interconnecting distant quantum nodes through photonic links. Extending such networks beyond metropolitan distances requires quantum repeaters to overcome the exponential attenuation of photons in optical fiber. Across all architectures, a key requirement is the indistinguishability of single photons, which directly impacts the fidelity of photonic operations based on two-photon interference, such as Bell-state measurements and fusion gates. Here, we demonstrate generation of highly indistinguishable single photons from a coherently excited tin-vacancy center in diamond, achieving raw Hong-Ou-Mandel interference visibilities exceeding 0.95. By separating intrinsic emitter properties from technical imperfections, we show that decoherence plays a negligible role and that the remaining limitations are predominantly technical in nature, arriving at an intrinsic indistinguishability of up to 0.999. We further show that quantum frequency conversion to the telecom C-band preserves the photon indistinguishability. In combination with the long-lived electron and nuclear spin coherence times, these results establish tin-vacancy centers in diamond as a competitive platform for long-distance quantum networks and photonic quantum information processing. We further substantiate this potential through Monte Carlo simulations of a quantum-repeater link, demonstrating that the SnV-center platform surpasses the bound set by direct transmission.
summary: The research demonstrates that tin-vacancy centers in diamond can generate single photons with extremely high indistinguishability ($\approx 0.999$). By meticulously separating emitter physics from technical noise sources, the authors establish this platform as a leading candidate for building long-distance quantum networks and photonic quantum information processors.
main_problem: The primary goal is demonstrating highly indistinguishable single photons from a tin-vacancy (SnV) spin qubit in diamond for use in long-distance quantum networks.
main_result: The authors achieved raw Hong-Ou-Mandel interference visibilities exceeding 0.95, establishing an intrinsic photon indistinguishability up to 0.999, even after frequency conversion to the telecom band.
method: Measurements involve characterizing single-photon purity using Hanbury-Brown-Twiss setups and measuring indistinguishability via Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, complemented by detailed noise modeling using TCSPC data.
model_or_system: The platform is the SnV center in diamond, acting as a solid-state quantum emitter. The work models photon generation fidelity, decoherence effects, and simulates performance improvements in quantum repeater links.
key_observables: Raw Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) interference visibilities (>0.95), intrinsic indistinguishability ($\approx 0.999$), single-photon purity ($g^{(2)}(0)$), and spectral linewidths ($\sim 30$ MHz).
important_parameters: Intrinsic indistinguishability, coherence times (electron/nuclear spin), temporal gating fractions (e.g., 65% of the wave packet), and frequency conversion efficiency.
main_assumptions: The analysis separates intrinsic emitter properties from technical imperfections, assuming that residual reflections are the main limitation to raw purity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Rabi oscillations, photoluminescence excitation spectra, $g^{(2)}(	au)$ measurements showing background subtraction, and comparisons of HOM visibility in visible versus telecom regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first demonstrating high single-photon purity from the SnV center, then quantifying indistinguishability via HOM interference, and finally extending this potential by showing preservation of indistinguishability after quantum frequency conversion to the telecom C-band for network applications.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete experimental metrics (high visibility, quantified intrinsic indistinguishability) crucial for assessing solid-state emitters as viable nodes in future quantum communication infrastructure, directly impacting photonic QI protocols.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: a, Photoluminescence excitation spectrum of a single SnV center recorded over 24 h. The average of all individual scans (solid black line) is fitted with a Lorentzian function (red dashed line), yielding a slightly power-broadened linewidth of 30.8(2) MHz. This value agrees with the linewidth obtained from a single scan, 30.7(4) MHz, indicating negligible spectral drift over the entire measurement duration. Furthermore the linewidth remains close to the Fourier-transform-limited value of 28.9(2) MHz expected from the measured excited-state lifetime of 5.68 ns. Fig. 2: a, Two-photon HOM interference of res- onantly excited photons with repetition period Trep = 77.5 ns and using the 93% time-gating window. Consecutive photons are overlapped in an unbalanced fiber-based MZI with orthogonal (black) or parallel (red) polarization. Comparison of the central peak areas yields a raw visibility of V raw,93% HOM = 0.950+0.006 −0.008. The grey shaded area represents the expected coincidence distribution for perfectly indistinguishable emitter photons, taking into account the measured background noise. b, Two-photon HOM interference after fre- quency conversion, resulting in a raw visibility of V raw,93% HOM = 0.80+0.01 −0.03.

Fig. 3: Raw two-photon interference visibility in the visible (red) and telecom (black) regime as a function of the remaining fraction of the photon wave packet after temporal gating of the detection window. The visibility is extracted from the raw coincidence counts by comparing the integrated area of the central peak to those of the far-delayed peaks. Shaded regions denote the 95% confidence interval, which increases for narrower gating win- dows due to reduced photon statistics.
